searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; one left unspent. Eight were restricted to a house's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: argiolas.it twice (Turriga; the family history), sellaemosca.com once (the Cuvée 161 sheet and the Torbato sheets), vinicontini.com twice (the history; the Antico Gregori and Riserva sheets), cantinadisantadi.it twice (the story; the Terre Brune sheets) and capichera.it four times (the origins; the VT sheet; the Capichera sheet and the swap; Vign'angena). Seven blocked the author's own sources so that a second, independent source would show (the Argiolas history twice, the Sella & Mosca history and the necropolis, the Vernaccia and Carignano del Sulcis decrees, the Santadi history, the Capichera wine). Three went to the appellation bodies' summaries (Sardegna Agricoltura for the Vernaccia di Oristano, Carignano del Sulcis and Vermentino di Gallura texts), one to the Ministry of Culture's museum pages on the goddess of Turriga, one to the soils of the Tirso valley, and the rest to the press and the merchants. The DOCG search served Contini, Santadi and Capichera alike and is counted with Capichera. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own pages and sheets for their own dates and methods and to the appellation bodies' texts, then to the press, the museums and the merchants, with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves.

Where the sources corrected the record (the age of the goddess of Turriga, the nursery's purpose, the gregori, the Riserva's four years, the Superiore's two years, Tachis at Santadi in the 1980s, the VT's picking and its months in barrique, Vign'angena's leased vineyards) the record was set right with its source; where a detail rested on no source the refuter read (some fifty years of bulk wine, the founder's death in 1936, marshy land, seven years of oak for Anghelu Ruju, calcareous Sulcis soils, the Sinis for Antico Gregori, Marchese di Villamarina long on its skins) it was cut or set as the sources give it.
Prices on the houses' shops and the merchants' pages, a ranking of Italian reds and hectares (Argiolas, Sella & Mosca) were read and not used.

tested: Founded 1938, the founder born in 1906 inheriting a small vineyard from his father, his death in 2009 past a hundred: the house's German history page (1938), its Turriga page (born 1906), Grapeguru and Falstaff (inherited about three hectares and founded the cellar in 1938; died in 2009 at 102): confirmed. The library's 1938 holds.

Turriga first harvested in 1988 and released in 1991, aged 18 to 24 months in French barriques and 12 to 14 in bottle: the house's Turriga page, WineBeBop and Dispensas: confirmed. The four grapes, Cannonau leading: the house's pages, Dispensas and the library: confirmed.

The site: the house names its Selegas estates (Selegas-Sa Tanca and Sisini) bought after 1979; a merchant's sheet in the results gives the Tenuta Turriga in agro di Selegas, Piscina Trigus, at 230 metres on mainly calcareous soils: confirmed, the word moderately cut.

The 1979 journey to Argentina and California: the house's pages give the founder travelling and then buying the Selegas estates; Grapeguru gives the founder's sons the journey. Changed to the family, as both accounts allow.

The mother goddess of Turriga: the Ministry of Culture's Cagliari museum pages and Preistoria in Italia give a marble statuette of the cruciform type found at Turriga on the border of Senorbì, Selegas and Ortacesus, of the late Neolithic (the Ozieri culture, given as 3000 to 2500 BC or the fourth to third millennium BC). More than five thousand years old is not what the archaeologists give; changed.
Bulk wine for some fifty years: Dispensas gives wine sold in bulk in the founder's day, and no source gives a span; changed to decades in the story and the question's stem.

Tachis from 1988: the sources read give Turriga developed in 1988 with Tachis, or from the late 1980s; none dates the start of his work with the house; changed to the late 1980s. His dates, 1933 to 2016, stand on the author's Wikipedia and Drinks Business, beside wide agreement.
The third generation taking the house on in 2003: the house's German page alone, primary for its own history: kept.

The house rules: the founder described, since his grandson of the same name is living; the grandchildren, the winemaker and the founder's sons met and not named; hectares (230, 280 or 600 acres) met and not used; no price, no score, no judging superlative, British, no dash. The questions: one key each, four options of a kind (four island grapes; four figures of Italian and French wine, all dead), the explanations teach.

tested: Founded in 1899 by an engineer of the Sella family and a lawyer of the Mosca family, both from Piedmont: Food and Wine Italia, Italian Wikipedia and Reporter Gourmet: confirmed. No dates found for either founder, so both stay described.

The nursery: the sources give a nursery of grafted vines (barbatelle) founded to restore the viticulture of Italy and Europe struck by phylloxera, one keeping it to the early 1950s; the vineyards of the mainland changed. The reclamation: Italian Wikipedia gives the clearing of boulders of sandstone, trachyte and limestone from I Piani, not the draining of a marsh; marshy cut.

Torbato: the house's Torbato sheet calls it a rare and precious variety rediscovered and rehabilitated by Sella & Mosca; one source in the results dates the recovery to the early 1980s and another says the house long grew and made it alone: the hedged claim confirmed, the rest left out as single sourced.
Campari in 2002 and Terra Moretti in 2016: Italian Wikipedia and the anniversary pieces: confirmed.

The necropolis of Anghelu Ruju found in 1903 on the estate's land, while stone was quarried for the new buildings, and dug by Antonio Taramelli from 1904; Ozieri culture, about 3200 to 2800 BC: Wikipedia and Musei Online: confirmed.

Cuvée 161: the house's sheet gives 24 hours of cold maceration at 10 degrees Celsius, soft pressing, cold settling and fermentation in temperature controlled steel, no malolactic, about six months on the lees in steel with 15 per cent in barrique; Vinissimus and Vino.com agree in outline: confirmed. The soils: calcareous, of ancient marine sedimentation, which name the Terre Bianche: confirmed. The house keeps separate pages for Terre Bianche and Terre Bianche Cuvée 161: the label term reworded.

Anghelu Ruju: the house's sheet as an importer reprints it gives Cannonau dried in the sun on reed mats for 15 to 20 days, covered at night; Xtrawine a fortified red of the Alghero DOC; no source gives a minimum of seven years in oak: changed.
Marchese di Villamarina was not searched; long on its skins is cut as resting on no source of the refuter's, Cabernet Sauvignon alone in barriques kept with the author's two sheets.

The house rules: the Terra Moretti owner, already in people.json, is not named; hectares (520, 550; Torbato 130 or 150) met and not used; no price, no score; British, no dash. The questions: four white grapes of Sardinia; four first uses of the land; one key each.

tested: Founded 1898 by Salvatore Contini: the house's history page (1898, the founder's flair for business, Vernaccia then the district's common wine) and the library: confirmed; the house's own Vernaccia page gives 1895, left open.

The founder's death in 1936 and the son's inheritance: the history page gives the son joining in the 1930s and taking over the running of the house on the eve of the Second World War; no source read gives 1936. Changed, and the founder, now without a date, is described rather than named.

The DOC of 1971: Sardegna Agricoltura gives the first DOC of Sardinia, recognised by a decree of 11 August 1971, and the Gazzetta Ufficiale of 30 September 1971 is cited beside it: confirmed. The Riserva: at least four years in cask (Sardegna Agricoltura, Assovini, the older text of the disciplinare): the label term made exact.

Antico Gregori: the house's page and sheet give a harvest in mid October, service at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius in a large glass, the 1991 aged about thirty three years and completed with small amounts of much older Vernaccia, above all the 1975; the Riserva sheet casks of oak and chestnut with flor: confirmed. The 1979 is on Xtrawine's and Callmewine's pages and the 1991 on Gambero Rosso's: confirmed.

The gregori: two papers in the proceedings of the Accademia Italiana della Vite e del Vino give them as the older soils of the rises around the lower Tirso, pebbly with tenacious clay or leached, of loam to clay loam, set against the bennaxi, the deep alluvial soils by the river; one merchant's page calls them poor and sandy. Lean and sandy changed to what the papers agree on. The same papers give the Sinis calcareous sedimentary soils, and no source ties Antico Gregori to the Sinis: cut.
Vermentino di Gallura a DOCG in 1996, in the second question's explanation: Sardegna Agricoltura and Assovini (decree of 11 September 1996): confirmed.

The house rules: the fourth generation met in the author's report and not named; no price, no score, no medal (the gold of 1912 at Milan, on the house's page alone, stays out); the reference in the story's close is a word of rank and is reworded; British, no dash. The questions: four ways of ageing, four years; one key each; the explanations teach.

tested: A co-operative founded in 1960: the co-operative's own pages and the library: confirmed.

The turn to quality: several secondaries give 1976, when a new president took on a co-operative in difficulty and turned it from quantity to quality, with wine sold in bulk until the 1980s: consistent with the middle of the 1970s.

Tachis: the co-operative's own story gives his first contact in the 1980s, after he came to Sardinia as consultant to the consortium of DOC wines; secondaries give 1976, 1980 or the early 1980s. The record had him brought in with the turn of the mid 1970s; changed to the 1980s by the co-operative's account.

Terre Brune first made in 1984: the co-operative's pages and secondaries: confirmed; two accounts give the 1984 vintage first released in 1988, left out. The first great Sardinian red aged in barrique is the co-operative's own claim, with secondaries repeating it: kept hedged.

The sheet: Carignano 95 per cent and Bovaleddu 5 per cent; hand picked from the end of September to the first or second ten days of October; about fifteen days in temperature controlled steel; an early malolactic that lets the wine into fine grained French barriques from early December, for about eighteen months; one version adds about twelve months in bottle; served at 18 degrees in a wide glass: confirmed.

Ungrafted bush vines: the co-operative's page on ungrafted vines and the merchants' sheets (Callmewine, Grandi Bottiglie): confirmed. Sand near the sea: the library and the region record; calcareous rests on no source read: cut.

The DOC: a decree of 1 June 1977 (Sardegna Agricoltura); at least 85 per cent Carignano; the Superiore from alberello or alberello appoggiato vines alone and aged at least two years, six months of them in bottle (the ministry's text and Assovini): confirmed, the ageing added to the label term.

The house rules: the co-operative's president and its oenologist met and not named; no price, no score (a ranking among Italy's reds met and not used); the reference red of the story's close reworded; British, no dash. The questions: four ways of growing or making; four years; one key each.

tested: The origins: the house's page gives the late 1970s for the turn to unblended Vermentino, the early 1980s for the house's whole turn to the grape, the name from caput erat, the wine called Capichera first made in 1980 and in 1990 the decision to vinify Vermentino alone in barriques, the house saying it was the first to promote barrique ageing of pure Vermentino: confirmed, hedged as the house's account.

The VT's making: the house's sheet gives the harvest in September, or early October in a late year, fermentation in steel at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius for about four weeks, four to six months of maturation and then bottle ageing, release no earlier than two years after the harvest; its VT page calls it Vermentino aged in barriques. The record's picked late is the wine's name, not the house's picking date; changed in the making, the label, the story, the trap, the card and the question.
The appellation: the house's general VT page and its 2023 page give Isola dei Nuraghi IGT, its 2024 page Vermentino di Gallura Superiore DOCG: kept as IGT, long used, and left open.

Vign'angena: the house's page gives other people's vineyard in Gallurese, made in the first years from vineyards the house worked under lease until its own came into bearing, first made in 1994 and fermented in steel alone (Winefully agrees on the steel): bought grapes changed to leased vineyards.
Santigaìni: K&L and Eurowines give it since 2003, one merchant the Coddu Ecchju vineyard at Arzachena, the house a cru released four years after the harvest: confirmed.
Vermentino di Gallura a DOCG in 1996 and the island's only one: Sardegna Agricoltura (decree of 11 September 1996), Assovini and Agraria.org: confirmed.

The swap: the house's own pages call the wine named Capichera its iconic wine and Winefully the estate's flagship; its sheet gives Vermentino alone, picked in September, fermented in steel at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius for four weeks, matured mainly in steel, service at 8 to 10 degrees Celsius and a high ageing potential; one merchant's page in the results calls it barrique aged, against the house's sheet, and one gives its first year as 1981, against the house's 1980.

The house rules: the family's members and the reported buyer met in the author's report and not named; prices met on the house's shop pages and not used; no score; British, no dash. The questions: four styles; four years; one key each.

swaps.why: The house's own pages call the Capichera its iconic wine and its first, made since 1980, and Winefully calls it the estate's flagship; the VT, made since 1990, is the barrique aged wine beside it, and the only source that ranks it first is the library's note of the estate's most discussed wine. The plan's own note asks for exactly this check, and the brief's ground for a swap, a flagship the house does not lead with, is met. Every fact of the swapped record stands on the house's own sheet for the Capichera (Vermentino alone, picked in September, steel at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius for four weeks, matured mainly in steel, 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, high ageing potential) or on facts the record already holds; a merchant's word that it is barrique aged and another's first year of 1981 are against the house's sheet and are not used. The house, the producerId and the key are kept, as in the Pfalz, Swartland and Mas Amiel rulings; no id of wave two is frozen. The VT moves to the head of others, with its dry, barrique aged teaching kept in a trap and a card.

patch.wine.name: Capichera
patch.wine.making: Picked in September, by the house's sheet, the Vermentino is fermented in stainless steel tanks at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius for about four weeks. It is then matured mainly in steel before bottling, without the barriques that shape the VT.
patch.wine.glass: Wild flowers, hawthorn and wisteria with rosemary, thyme and lavender, yellow fleshed fruit and flint; dry, lively and full, with a long, saline finish.
patch.wine.ageing: Fresh and open on release, it holds and deepens for some years in bottle; the house gives it a high ageing potential.
patch.wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, as the house advises; no need to decant; a white wine glass of medium size.

wine.label.means: The old name of the family estate, from the Latin caput erat, it was the capital, as the house tells it.
Sardinia's island wide geographic indication, which the house long used in place of the Gallura DOCG.

patch.table: The Capichera is the estate's own Vermentino from the granite of the Gallura, made since 1980 and the wine the house puts first: fermented in steel and matured mainly there, it is dry, lively and saline, with wild flowers, rosemary and flint. Pour it at 8 to 10 degrees.
story:replace: For a sommelier the VT shows Vermentino of the Gallura with weight, oak and years in bottle, and a candidate must remember that late harvest here means dry.

For a sommelier the Capichera is where the estate began and the wine it puts first, Vermentino of the Gallura with weight and years in bottle, while the VT beside it is aged in barriques and dry despite its name.

swapNote: One swap proposed, by the author; accepted with its patch. No other pick is in doubt: Argiolas, Sella & Mosca, Attilio Contini and Cantina Santadi are the houses the region record and the library name, each with the wine the house itself leads with.
planNotes: argiolas: the note is answered: the first harvest of 1988 and the release of 1991 (the house, WineBeBop, Dispensas), Cannonau with Carignano, Bovale Sardo and Malvasia Nera, the label Isola dei Nuraghi IGT. The why stands.

sella-mosca: the why's first as a nursery of rootstocks is better first as a nursery of grafted vines, the barbatelle, by the sources read; its a grape the house long grew almost alone rests on one source in the refuter's results as in the author's, and the record does not repeat it. The note is answered: the record teaches Terre Bianche Cuvée 161, which the house keeps beside a plain Terre Bianche.

contini: the why's blended from very old reserves holds for the older bottlings and in part for the vintage dated ones (the 1991 completed with much older Vernaccia, above all the 1975); the note is answered: recent releases carry a vintage and the label reads Vernaccia di Oristano DOC Riserva.
santadi: the note is answered: 1984 for the first Terre Brune, Carignano with about a twentieth of Bovaleddu. The why stands.

capichera: the swap above; the note is answered: the house puts the Capichera first, and its labels read Isola dei Nuraghi IGT until the 2024 vintage, when its pages give Vermentino di Gallura Superiore DOCG.
